x: Paul Coates will have a good saason if he can get his leg right while our younger ranks have been growing apace with Paul Duckett and Andy Hinchcliff showing particular promise.
The Olympic Cup was won by Carl Lawton from a fast improving Paul Duckett. Andy Hinchcliff( who has six more years in this championship) revenged an earlier defeat by Vic Butcher to finish fourth.

Andy Hinchcliff recorded a good 27.13 in the Youth 3 Miles and in the 6 miles Brian Ward finished sixth with some strong walking. The 10,000 metres was held on the track which was not in much of a state for fast walking.
Nearly a clean sweep for Belgrave in the Surrey County Track Walks. The senior was won by Paul Nihill from Wil Wesch, Paul Duckett took the junior and Andy Hinchcliff walked off with the youth title.

On the home front Paul Duckett and Andy Hinchcliff have both produced some good races in preperation for the winter with Paul's 24.50 for fourth place in the English Schools 5,000 Metres being a particularly creditable performance.

Andy Hinchcliff walked well to record 26:45 finishing 11th while McAnally can reckon he's in the top thirty with a plucky 31.01. In the Junior Five Mile Race our only starter Paul Duckett banged in a useful 41.08.
Lack of competition did not prevent Paul Duckett from turning in a useful 42:12 to win this championship. Andy Hinchcliff, 3 years younger than Paul, took the silver medal and broke 47 minutes.
